P1.evidence: Referenced the application but only in passing rather than reading it back — 'I read through your application. I have a somewhat of a head start on things' plus 'I saw you're a consultant or something'. Full four-part frame delivered: 'get a super solid understanding of where you're at in your fitness journey, what you're looking to accomplish, where the gap is... and from there, we can kind of map out what a potential coaching program could look like for you.' Frame agreement taken with 'That all sound good?' and open question run: 'What do you feel we could potentially help you with?'

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight asked directly at 00:12:39. Training week asked and pinned down — 'walk me through what a typical week looks like in terms of movement' followed by 'right now it sounds like it's maybe two though'. Diet asked at 00:16:29. Work only half-covered: he confirmed semi-retirement but never established desk-bound versus on-feet. The whole medical picture — PTSD, three failed leg surgeries, popliteal entrapment, rotator cuff, sedating medication — was volunteered unprompted and never asked for, so P2c and P2d score miss under the volunteered-information rule. Sleep and energy were likewise volunteered ('I've just been sleeping in until like 10 or 11 because I can't sleep until 2 or 3 at night') and never asked about or followed up. Results from current training also volunteered, never asked.

P3.evidence: Surface layer is thin: 'what's the ultimate goal with your fitness then?' substitutes for the one-thing-you'd-change question, and the mobility/strength/energy menu and the something-physical-you-can't-do question were never asked — a real omission given three failed leg surgeries. The deep layer is where this call is strong. Bridge run cleanly: 'why is it important for you to get down to that weight and maintain, like, what's the actual drive or motivation behind it?' Drove hard to kids, legacy and identity: 'what does that also do to them when they see that, hey, you put responsibility externally.' Reflected back explicitly: 'I don't think this is just a fitness conversation, man. And I think you know that, too.'

P4.evidence: Past attempts were never asked for — the PT, Ozempic, battle ropes and the repeated cycles were all volunteered. But root cause was worked properly: 'why do you feel like we're not able to maintain consistency?' then 'what's it going to take for us to be consistent, man? Like, what do we actually need to get in place'. The prospect named the gap himself — 'usually accountability is a part of it' — and the rep ran the information-isn't-the-problem move well, taking permission first ('do I have your permission to speak like super directly with you?') and then landing 'as soon as that accountability goes away, well, that means all your results go away' and 'no one can do it for you, man.'

P5.evidence: All four moves ran in order. 'If we continue letting that happen, what does life actually look like in the next two, three, four, five years?' Answer: 'Well, it's the same.' Then the settle-for test as devil's advocate — 'What's so bad about that? Why not just stay the same?' — which produced the kids and the purpose material. Line in the sand asked directly at 00:33:45: 'do you feel like it's actually time to draw a line in the sand and actually figure this thing out?'

P6.evidence: Neither commitment question was asked. Worse, the answer to the line-in-the-sand question was an explicit hesitation — 'I draw lines in the sand and then I'll, you know, scuff them out when I get there... I've done the cycles quite a few times' — which per P6c required a return to Phase 5. Instead the rep offered reassurance ('I think you need to give yourself some grace') and moved straight into presenting the pillars with no verbal yes on the table.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. The call ended at 00:55 for a dentist appointment after only two of the three pillars had been delivered; no price, tiers, agreement or onboarding step arose.

objection_plays.detail: Fear/doubt landed squarely at 00:34:18 — he has hit the goal before and always regressed, so what he is really doubting is himself. The rep responded with an unscripted Tony Robbins baby-learning-to-walk analogy, which does the same job as the scripted BRIDGE and PLANE reframes and was well delivered. But none of the scripted moves ran: no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?', no pleasure-versus-pain question, no 'how will you know if you never actually try?' And the play was never closed out — he was left having neither accepted nor rejected the reframe.

A clinical-fit objection was raised in the prospect's very first substantive answer: 'I wonder if them, or if they are okay. I've got a rota cuff injury.' There is no scripted play for this — it is the known gap in the script, the same one flagged against this prospect elsewhere in the corpus. The rep improvised a capability claim ('we can not only work around injuries', 'Trevor constantly updates your program') and an outcome claim about other injured clients ending up in less pain. He never asked the screening question the situation demanded: has any clinician cleared you for loaded ballistic kettlebell work. This is a script gap, not solely a rep failure, but the improvisation ran toward selling rather than toward screening.

notes: Phases 4 and 5 are genuinely strong — the permission-to-be-direct move, the crown quote and the consequence frame did real work on a hard prospect. The coachable failure is the seam between them and the presentation: the prospect answered the line-in-the-sand question with an explicit 'I always scuff it out' and the rep presented anyway, with no commitment check at all. Baseline is the other gap — every medical fact in this call arrived unprompted, which is exactly how a rotator cuff injury and three failed leg surgeries end up unscreened.
